source_row.rationale: H2 receptor blockers reduce gastric acid secretion by blocking histamine H2 receptors on stomach parietal cells, while PPIs work through a different, generally more potent and longer-lasting mechanism by directly and more completely inhibiting the proton pump (H+/K+ ATPase) responsible for acid secretion, making PPIs generally more effective for significant acid suppression.
source_row.source_detail: Mechanism section: PPIs inhibit gastric H+/K+ ATPase; contrasted with H2 receptor antagonists that block histamine H2 signaling; StatPearls; accessed 2026-08-14.
